one_line: Agent-assisted lost-property matching with private proof and human-controlled release.
what_it_does: Structures public loss reports, finds privacy-safe candidate matches, and routes proof, review, credential, and handoff decisions through bounded human checkpoints.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially changes the workflow by exposing typed, state-dependent matching and aggregate reads while deliberately omitting sensitive proof and approval actions; a general UI-driving agent would be less reliable and riskier.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe opaque candidate handles, aggregate state, bounded tools, and human-only proof/approval/handoff.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows an agent collaboration panel and find_candidate_matches alongside the staged workflow.
execution_rationale: The detailed lifecycle is coherent and the submitted video transcript claims end-to-end state transitions, though frame evidence did not clearly show final completion.
execution_evidence: 170-second video transcript covers draft, matching, role switch, staff review, approval, one-time credential, atomic handoff, and tool removal.
Contact sheets visibly show a consistent ClaimGate/Lost report desk and private evidence workflow.
Visual evidence does not clearly show a conclusive final match or handoff receipt.
impact_rationale: Lost-property desks have a concrete privacy and accountability problem, and the separation of public clues from private ownership proof is a credible solution.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies lost-property search and human release decisions.
Packaging visibly presents Report, Match, Prove, Review, Pickup and aggregate-only evidence state.
creativity_rationale: The privacy-preserving division between agent preparation and human proof/release is a thoughtful, memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Private proof remains manual while the agent receives only bounded aggregate/candidate information.
Role-aware continuation and one-time credential handoff extend the concept beyond a basic search form.
usability_note: Clear staged workflow and visible human checkpoints; evidence suggests a usable desk flow, with some final-state uncertainty.
red_flags: Final completion and privacy enforcement are primarily claimed rather than independently observable in the available frame sheets.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary: aggregate agent reads without exposing private proof.
State-dependent tool lifecycle and human release control.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage, concrete impact, and unusually coherent safety boundary; advance despite incomplete visible final-state proof.

one_line: Shared planner for module-level self-hosting profiles, capacity checks, and read-only CLI handoffs.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents select module profiles, declare CPU/RAM/storage, assess declared capacity, and prepare reviewable commands or Markdown handoffs without executing them.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured planner state and validated read-only operations improve precision and repeatability, but a general agent could achieve much of the same UI outcome with moderate friction.
leverage_evidence: About text names four narrow tools sharing implementation and planner state with the human UI.
Contact sheets visibly show module planning and capacity declaration states, but no legible tool invocation.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and the planner appears coherent, with profile selection, capacity assessment, and handoff states represented; agent execution is not visibly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and about text specifies explicit controls, below-minimum blocking, and read-only handoff.
Contact sheets show consistent planner screens, validation indicators, and capacity/handoff workflow.
impact_rationale: Self-hosters face real resource-fit and configuration problems; honest declared-capacity checks and module-level alternatives provide credible practical value.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets self-hosted infrastructure planning.
Visible captions emphasize precise capacity controls and seeing limits before handoff.
creativity_rationale: Module-level compute profiles combined with a human-agent shared planning state is a fresh, useful synthesis for infrastructure setup.
creativity_evidence: Independent profile choices avoid one global tier.
Read-only CLI handoff preserves reviewability rather than giving an agent shell access.
usability_note: Structured controls and transparent validation appear approachable; repetitive frames leave some interaction details unclear.
red_flags: No submitted video and no visible agent/tool invocation in frame sheets.
Capacity assessment is explicitly declared-capacity, not host compatibility.
advance_reason: Solid practical product with meaningful shared-state WebMCP value, though weaker evidence and novelty than the top projects.

one_line: Agentic web workspace where agents discover capabilities and collaborate with humans on shared artifacts.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP tools to search, compare, calculate, propose, organize, save, and export results in a collaborative canvas with an Agent View.
leverage_rationale: The concept makes structured website capabilities and shared artifacts central to agent-human collaboration, beyond ordinary page reading or UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly centers capability discovery, structured actions, Agent View, and shared canvas artifacts.
No frame sheets or video were submitted to verify the claimed interaction.
execution_rationale: The concept is broad but the packet supplies only sparse text and packaging, with no runtime frames or video evidence; end-to-end completion is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and Devpost page exists.
No submitted video or frame sheets; about text contains substantial whitespace and incomplete-looking presentation.
impact_rationale: A shared workspace for agents and people addresses a broad, credible interaction problem, but the packet does not demonstrate the value in practice.
impact_evidence: Example goal is a constrained weekend plan with search, comparison, budgeting, and export.
About text articulates the limitation of agents merely understanding pages.
creativity_rationale: The shared web workspace and Agent View propose an ambitious agent-native interaction model rather than a single automated action.
creativity_evidence: Product concept treats websites as environments where agents work alongside users.
Collaborative canvas and artifact lifecycle are an ambitious extension of WebMCP.
usability_note: The intended workflow is understandable, but there is no visual runtime evidence to assess actual usability.
red_flags: Sparse/whitespace-heavy packet and broad claims make completeness difficult to assess.
advance_reason: Interesting concept, but missing runtime evidence caps execution and leaves eligibility and core behavior unclear.

one_line: Authenticated sites expose safe structured drafting and exact previews while humans retain publishing control.
what_it_does: Stages coordinated CMS edits, validates schemas and policies, prepares image handoffs, renders production-faithful previews, and atomically publishes only after human approval.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: the authenticated site exposes precise, permission-aware, reversible operations over shared live state, while intentionally withholding publish. Generic UI automation cannot match this reliability and safety as readily.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies twelve purpose-built tools, revision IDs, permissions, validation, persistent changesets, and no publish tool.
180-second video is reported and demo is alive, though no transcript was supplied.
execution_rationale: The claimed workflow is unusually complete and internally coherent, covering draft, validation, exact preview, approval/rejection, atomic publication, receipt, and restoration.
execution_evidence: About text describes coordinated homepage/pricing/FAQ edits and production-component previews.
Human-only Approve & publish/Reject draft boundary and immutable receipt form a complete lifecycle.
impact_rationale: Content teams and site owners have a real need for faster edits without granting agents unsafe production publishing power.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets authenticated website editing and publishing safety.
Workflow addresses credentials, permissions, schemas, preview fidelity, and reversible changes.
creativity_rationale: The agent-native CMS framing and exact same-renderer preview with human publication gate is a strong, original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Structured edits and revision freshness are handled by the application rather than inferred from source/UI.
No publish tool and atomic receipt make the safety model concrete.
usability_note: Clear author-workspace flow and preview/approve boundary should be understandable; login adds expected friction.
red_flags: No public repository and no transcript; exact runtime behavior is less independently inspectable.
advance_reason: High-leverage, credible agent-native CMS workflow with strong completeness and impact.

one_line: Football review room where coaches draw tactical intent and agents search synchronized match evidence.
what_it_does: Reads pitch drawings and queries a complete match across events, tracking, video, and sequences, then synchronizes selected evidence across views.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent consume live visual workspace semantics and return precise, inspectable evidence; translating a coach's drawing into coordinates and database filters through UI driving would be substantially worse.
leverage_evidence: About text says the coach draws zones/routes and the agent reads live workspace state.
Contact sheet visibly shows video, timeline, tactical pitch, an execution-like overlay, and synchronized result.
execution_rationale: A focused workflow is coherently represented from visual query to synchronized video/pitch/timeline evidence, though some labels and full search lifecycle are not legible.
execution_evidence: About text specifies 44:55 first half, 1,029 actions, route/moment/pattern searches, comparison, and review tray.
Contact sheet visibly demonstrates cross-view synchronization to one observed moment.
impact_rationale: Coaches and analysts have a clear real need to search complex match footage using tactical concepts rather than database terminology.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies coach-agent football review and inspectable evidence.
Visible result aligns video, timeline, and spatial pitch around a selected play.
creativity_rationale: Using a tactical drawing as the shared language for agent search is genuinely novel and memorable, with depth across spatial, temporal, and event evidence.
creativity_evidence: Coach brings spatial judgement while agent performs search.
Route, zone, temporal-chain, comparison, and synchronized evidence interactions pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: The pitch-as-query interaction is direct for football users; dense analysis may require onboarding.
standouts: Visual tactical language directly drives structured agent search.
Inspectability across video, tracking, events, and pitch.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with strong visible end-to-end evidence.

one_line: Shared procurement workspace where buyers and agents revise sourcing decisions together.
what_it_does: Loads a fictional supplier case, lets agents propose shortlist and negotiation changes, and lets buyers revise and feed the shared state back to the agent.
leverage_rationale: Shared live sourcing state and structured proposal/revision exchange are useful improvements, but comparable outcomes are possible through a normal dashboard plus agent UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent reads, direct workspace updates, AGENT PROPOSAL, HUMAN-REVISED state, and adaptation.
No video or frame sheets were submitted.
execution_rationale: The central proposal-revision loop is coherent on paper, but the packet has no visual or video proof of the workflow.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and the about text gives a concrete three-supplier, five-dimension case.
No submitted video, frame sheets, or gallery images.
impact_rationale: Procurement decisions involve real tradeoffs and accountability; a shared state for constraints and negotiation planning is credible value for buyers.
impact_evidence: Concrete delivery, continuity, shortlist, and price-premium example.
Pitch targets procurement decision workspaces.
creativity_rationale: Human-revised agent proposals in procurement are a competent and useful angle, but the interaction model is less novel than the strongest entries.
creativity_evidence: Explicit HUMAN-REVISED state and adaptive negotiation plan.
Concept remains a familiar shared decision dashboard pattern.
usability_note: The proposal/revision statuses suggest a clear workflow, but no visual evidence is available.
red_flags: No video, frame sheets, or gallery images; execution and eligibility are therefore weakly evidenced.
standouts: Concrete human-revision loop over sourcing constraints.
advance_reason: Credible use case but insufficient evidence to advance against better-demonstrated projects.

one_line: Programmable world where an agent must invent, certify, and safely invoke a new WebMCP repair tool.
what_it_does: Agents learn ArkScript, author and test thermal policies, pass counterfactual and canary gates, then receive a dynamically registered tool able to repair canonical state.
leverage_rationale: The product's core challenge is impossible without dynamic structured agent capability: the agent must create, certify, receive, and invoke a new tool under live state and safety gates.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies eight initial tools, no repair capability, runtime ninth-tool registration, certification, canary, and revocation.
228-second video and multiple frame sheets are submitted.
execution_rationale: The deterministic world, extensive tests, delayed horizon, invariants, replay verification, and tool lifecycle describe a deeply pursued, coherent game loop.
execution_evidence: Concrete simulation scale: 766 cells, 4 networks, 127 fractures, 5 critical systems, 64 counterfactuals, 16-world canary.
Submitted 228-second demo supports claimed staged lifecycle, though transcript is absent.
impact_rationale: As an experimental game and agent-safety sandbox it offers credible learning and exploration value, though the audience/problem is narrower than practical workflow products.
impact_evidence: Playable objective and visible certification/canary mechanics turn protocol ideas into an experiential sandbox.
Impact is primarily educational/experimental rather than operational.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic tool invention, proof, earning, canarying, revocation, and canonical authority form an exceptionally original interaction model pursued at ambitious depth.
creativity_evidence: A new WebMCP tool is born only after executable counterexamples, invariants, replay, bounds, and zero-day canary.
The world metaphor makes protocol evolution and safety memorable.
usability_note: Strongly structured game loop, but ArkScript and multi-stage certification create substantial learning complexity.
standouts: Runtime creation and revocation of a capability.
advance_reason: Most ambitious and WebMCP-native concept in the packet, with unusually deep execution claims and strong video evidence.

one_line: Human-owned ritual ledger where an agent reads patterns and drafts reviews but cannot commit them.
what_it_does: Captures daily/weekly reflections, supplies bounded context to an agent, drafts pattern-aware reviews, and requires the person to commit the record.
leverage_rationale: Shared bounded context and a deliberate human commit boundary improve reliability and ownership, though a general agent could perform much of the drafting with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text explicitly define read/draft versus human commit boundary.
Frame sheets show repeated product/workflow states, but no legible tool invocation.
execution_rationale: The product has a focused ritual and a clear boundary, with multiple visual states suggesting a coherent daily/weekly flow; end-to-end agent use is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: About text explains daily questions, weekly review, deferred-commitment pattern detection, and visible draft commitment.
Five gallery images and submitted frame sheets provide packaging and UI evidence.
impact_rationale: People seeking accountability have a real need for reflection that preserves authorship; the ritual framing addresses a gap in capture-focused habit apps.
impact_evidence: Specific audience/problem narrative around accountability and repeated deferred commitments.
Product preserves human ownership by refusing to let the agent write the final record.
creativity_rationale: The insight that outsourced accountability becomes a report, encoded as a hard human-commit boundary, is a distinctive interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Agent performs retrospective reading and drafting but stops before decision/commit.
Daily and weekly ritual structure pursues the ownership idea coherently.
usability_note: A small, repeatable ritual and visible draft/commit boundary should be approachable.
red_flags: No video; agent tool use is claimed but not clearly visible in supplied frame evidence.
standouts: Specific ritual rather than generic productivity automation.
advance_reason: Clear audience need, memorable human-control insight, and coherent product scope justify advancing.

one_line: Audit dashboard where analysts and agents inspect power-market forecasts and immutable evidence.
what_it_does: Tracks timestamped forecasts, outcomes, missed days, provenance, and evaluation rules while agents and analysts audit the same ledger.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared access to forecast/evidence state supports reliable audit and provenance, but the core dashboard outcome could be reached through conventional UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch names six site tools and shared audit state.
About text emphasizes cutoff rules, immutable forecasts, and information availability; frame sheets provide dashboard evidence but no clearly legible tool trace.
execution_rationale: The evidence model and evaluation boundary are unusually explicit and coherent, with dashboard screenshots and described successful audit flow.
execution_evidence: About text specifies pre-auction timestamping, no future information, missed-day recording, and immutable forecast scoring.
Four gallery images and frame sheets visibly present track record, provenance, and audit views.
impact_rationale: Energy-market analysts and forecasting practitioners have a real need for honest, reproducible track records and evidence auditability.
impact_evidence: Specific German day-ahead electricity forecasting use case.
Visible protocol/provenance and weakest-days audit framing.
creativity_rationale: Forecast accountability and provenance are a meaningful angle on an analytics dashboard, though the underlying category is established.
creativity_evidence: Pre-registered evaluation rules and missed-day preservation make honesty a product feature.
Agent and analyst audit the same evidence ledger.
usability_note: Audit-oriented hierarchy appears useful for analysts, though domain specificity increases onboarding cost.
red_flags: No video and limited direct evidence of agent invocation.
standouts: Concrete power-market domain and evaluation discipline.
advance_reason: Well-evidenced, credible niche analytics product with strong execution and trustworthy audit design.

one_line: Safety-bounded emergency robot simulation with human approval for one exact rescue mission.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect hazards, coordinate four robots, validate routes against safety rules, then execute once after human approval and lose the temporary tool.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP encodes mission-scoped authority and dynamic execute capability; the agent cannot move robots until human approval and loses control after one mission, a boundary UI driving cannot reliably provide.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies seven planning tools, human-only approval, temporary eighth execute_rescue_mission, and removal after use.
Frame sheets are submitted, though no video transcript.
execution_rationale: The lifecycle and eleven-rule validation are concrete and coherent, with a clear simulated mission and receipt, though evidence is primarily claimed and frame-based.
execution_evidence: About text describes hazard scan, four specialist robots, route testing, approval, execution, receipt, and reset to seven tools.
Submitted frame sheets and Devpost packaging show the rescue simulation workflow.
impact_rationale: Emergency coordination is a high-value setting for exploring agent capability with strict human authority and mission containment, even as a simulation.
impact_evidence: Concrete scenario has trapped workers, fire, hazardous container, and four coordinated specialist robots.
Human approves exact rescue before movement and agent authority ends at mission completion.
creativity_rationale: The firebreak metaphor and mission-scoped tool lifecycle make a compelling, original safety interaction for multi-agent physical coordination.
creativity_evidence: 7 tools → human approval → one execute tool → return to 7 is a memorable capability boundary.
Four-role robot coordination and eleven safety checks pursue the idea beyond a toy button.
usability_note: The staged approval and receipt flow is clear; multi-robot planning may be cognitively dense.
red_flags: No video submitted; runtime and agent invocation are less directly verified than the concept suggests.
advance_reason: High-leverage safety design and memorable ambitious simulation merit advancement despite absent video.
